problem: Which of the following diagrams represents the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{y}{xy+1}\,i+\frac{x}{xy+1}\,j$ at the indicated points?
worked_solution:
We have to sketch the vector field at the points $(-2,0),(1,-2),$ and $(0,2).$

To sketch the vector field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the function $F(x,y)=\frac{y}{xy+1}\,i+\frac{x}{xy+1}\,j\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(-2,0) & =\frac{0}{(-2)(0)+1}\,i+\frac{-2}{(-2)(0)+1}\,j=-2\,j \\ F(1,-2) & =\frac{-2}{(1)(-2)+1}\,i+\frac{1}{(1)(-2)+1}\,j=2\,i-j \\ F(0,2) & =\frac{2}{(0)(2)+1}\,i+\frac{0}{(0)(2)+1}\,j=2\,i\end{aligned}
$$

We now draw our vectors. At each point, we draw the vector associated with that point, placing the tail end of the vector on the point itself. This gives the following diagram.
